# Claims and evidence

*CC BY 4.0 · v0.3 · Every material claim the project makes, with its evidence and limits. Status: **Implemented** (code and passing tests), **Demonstrated** (reproducible run whose evidence is generated by a documented command), **Designed** (specified, not implemented), **Planned** (future milestone), **Blocked** (needs an external decision or input), **Unverified** (stated but not validated in this iteration). If a sentence in the README or the white paper is not covered here, treat it as unverified.*

Common commands: `T-py` = `cd tools && python -m pytest -q`; `T-sol` = `cd contracts && npx hardhat test`; `DEMO` = `./examples/e2e/run.sh`, which writes `evidence-manifest.json`. CI evidence for the v0.3 branch: run [42644820168](https://github.com/xcapit/verifiable-policy-registry/actions/runs/42644820168) on `de5e039` (all four jobs passing); later runs on the PR supersede it.

Nivoli |
| C02 | Only the governor publishes versions, rotates the governor and assigns issuer roles | Implemented | `onlyGovernor` | `T-sol` | The governor is expected to be a Safe; Safe configuration is out of scope of these tests | M. Nivoli |
| C03 | A scope id belongs to the address that created it: `scopeId = keccak256(abi.encode(governor, name))`, so a canonical name cannot be front-run | Implemented, Demonstrated | `createScope`, `scopeIdOf`; shared vector in `T-sol` and `T-py` | `T-sol`; `DEMO` "no front-running" | Another address can still create a scope with a familiar name under its own id; verifiers pin governors from the deployment manifest (format implemented, VPR-049) | M. Nivoli |
| C04 | Appeals store only a document hash; rejection needs a reasoned-decision hash; a rejected document can be resubmitted | Implemented, Demonstrated | `fileAppeal`, `rejectAppeal`, `appealIdOf` | `T-sol`; `DEMO` appeal stages | Timeliness and fairness of decisions are institutional | Governor |
| C05 | One attestation role per address per scope, the governor cannot hold a role, and an EAS schema resolver accepts an attestation only from the role holder at issuance time | Implemented, Demonstrated | `setIssuer`, `issuerRole`, `IssuerRoleResolver` | `T-sol`; `DEMO` "resolver rejects the operator" | Schemas are not registered on a public network; one institution could still use several addresses (governance control) | M. Nivoli |
| C06 | The registry accepts policy changes only from the governor address; threshold authorisation exists only if that address is an m-of-n multisig | Implemented (access control); Designed and Blocked (threshold deployment) | `onlyGovernor`; proposed Safe configuration | `T-sol` covers registry access control only | The contract accepts an EOA as governor, in which case one key can act alone; deployment needs confirmed signers | Signers at Gate A |
| C07 | Policy changes, reasons, appeal status and contractual expiry are visible; enforcement after expiry and external recourse are deployment rules | Implemented (record and expiry signal); Designed (resolver behaviour, charter, recourse) | Registry; [policy governance](GOVERNANCE.md) | `DEMO` shows the contract reporting the policy out of force | A colluding majority can censor until expiry, and a resolver could continue an expired policy; no on-chain remedy ([threat model T16](security/THREAT_MODEL.md)) | Governor |
